name: Saturn's Rings from Voyager 1, November 3, 1980
blurb: Saturn's rings, made of billions of chunks of ice and rock. Seen by Voyager 1's narrow-angle camera through orange, green and blue filters: visible light only, 0.48 to 0.62 µm.
story: Saturn's Rings in sunlight, 9 days before Voyager 1's closest approach to Saturn on November 12, 1980. The ring particles range from tiny, dust-sized icy grains to chunks as big as a house.
